# Agent catalog

111 agents in 11 department plugins. Install a department with `/plugin install <department>@clawmain`.

## Agent Ops (`agent-ops`, 11 agents)

Run agents as a disciplined loop: plan, verify, reflect, budget, route handoffs, and learn from failures.

| Agent | Stage | Why | Mission |
|---|---|---|---|
| `loop-planner` | plan | clear finish line | Produce a plan that another agent could execute without asking questions: what done looks like, how to prove it, and the cheapest path there. |
| `loop-verifier` | verify | evidence over claims | Separate 'done' from 'said to be done'. Every criterion gets a verdict backed by output or file:line evidence. |
| `loop-reflector` | reflect | learn each iteration | Stop loops that spin. Look at what changed since the last iteration and choose the smallest next move that increases evidence of progress. |
| `budget-controller` | plan | spend on purpose | Make spend a decision, not an accident. Give each step a budget and a cheaper fallback. |
| `handoff-router` | plan | right agent next | Keep chains short and briefs complete: one next agent, with the context it needs and nothing else. |
| `stop-condition-judge` | reflect | know when stop | Apply the stop rules strictly and explain the verdict in one line. |
| `failure-analyst` | reflect | fix root causes | Explain why it failed, not just what failed, and propose one change that addresses the cause. |
| `memory-curator` | reflect | remember what matters | Only verified, reusable, non-obvious facts earn a line in agent memory; everything else is trimmed. |
| `skill-extractor` | reflect | repeatable workflows | Turn repetition into a skill once, so the next run is predictable and cheaper. |
| `agent-auditor` | verify | agents stay sharp | Grade each agent definition against the clawmain rubric and say exactly what to change. |
| `eval-designer` | verify | measure, not guess | Make agent quality measurable with the fewest cases that still catch real regressions. |

## AI Engineering (`ai-engineering`, 10 agents)

Build LLM-powered product features that hold up: evals, prompts, RAG, tool schemas, guardrails, cost, and context design.

| Agent | Stage | Why | Mission |
|---|---|---|---|
| `llm-eval-builder` | verify | measure model quality | Make every LLM feature testable with a small, representative dataset and graders that catch real failures. |
| `prompt-engineer` | act | clear instructions win | Rewrite prompts so behavior is specified, not hoped for, and prove the rewrite with evals. |
| `rag-reviewer` | verify | retrieve right context | Find which stage of the RAG pipeline loses the answer, with evidence from real queries. |
| `hallucination-checker` | verify | grounded answers only | Separate what the model was given from what it made up, claim by claim. |
| `llm-cost-estimator` | plan | know unit cost | Put a number on cost per request and per month, and show the cheapest changes that keep quality. |
| `tool-schema-designer` | act | tools models understand | Tool definitions a model can choose and call correctly on the first try. |
| `guardrail-designer` | plan | fail safe | Put checks where an LLM feature can fail badly, sized to the actual risk. |
| `agent-architect` | plan | simplest agent works | Choose the simplest agent design that meets the requirements, and make its loop, tools, and limits explicit. |
| `prompt-regression-tester` | verify | no silent regressions | Catch quality drops from prompt or model changes before users do. |
| `context-engineer` | plan | context is budget | Give the model exactly what it needs per call, ordered for attention and capped by a budget. |

## Architecture (`architecture`, 10 agents)

Map, protect, and evolve the structure of a codebase: modules, dependencies, boundaries, interfaces, data models, and migrations.

| Agent | Stage | Why | Mission |
|---|---|---|---|
| `module-mapper` | plan | faster navigation | Give a newcomer or an agent a one-screen map that answers 'where does X live?' without reading the whole repo. |
| `dependency-grapher` | plan | see real coupling | Show how modules actually depend on each other, so refactors and boundaries are based on the real import graph, not the folder names. |
| `boundary-enforcer` | verify | layers stay clean | Turn the intended architecture into rules a machine checks on every change, and report today's violations. |
| `refactor-planner` | plan | small safe steps | Make big refactors boring: every step compiles, passes tests, and could ship on its own. |
| `interface-designer` | plan | hard to misuse | Design interfaces that are small, hard to misuse, and stable, starting from how callers will actually call them. |
| `data-model-reviewer` | verify | integrity by design | Catch data-model mistakes while they are still cheap: missing constraints, wrong types, and indexes that do not match the queries. |
| `scalability-reviewer` | verify | works at scale | Find the first thing that breaks when traffic or data grows, and the cheapest fix for it. |
| `migration-planner` | plan | zero-downtime changes | Move systems and data from old to new without downtime or data loss, with a verified rollback at every phase. |
| `monorepo-organizer` | plan | packages stay independent | Keep a monorepo fast and understandable: clear package roles, one way to run tasks, and builds that touch only what changed. |
| `tech-stack-advisor` | plan | fit over hype | Pick the option that fits this repo and team today, and say plainly what it costs and what would change the answer. |

## Code Review (`code-review`, 10 agents)

Focused review lenses for diffs and PRs: each agent checks one concern and returns file:line findings with severity.

| Agent | Stage | Why | Mission |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bug-hunter` | verify | catch bugs early | Find the defects that would cause wrong behavior in production, with a concrete failing scenario for each. |
| `api-contract-reviewer` | verify | keep promises | Nothing a consumer relies on should change silently. |
| `concurrency-reviewer` | verify | races hide well | Find interleavings that corrupt data or hang, and describe each as a concrete sequence of events. |
| `error-handling-reviewer` | verify | fail loudly, safely | Every failure should be either handled on purpose or surfaced clearly, never silently lost. |
| `performance-reviewer` | verify | slow is broken | Find changes whose cost grows with data size or traffic, and estimate how much. |
| `readability-reviewer` | verify | code is read | Flag the few changes that most hurt the next reader, judged against this repo's own conventions. |
| `simplifier` | act | less to break | Make the same behavior take less code and fewer concepts, with tests as proof. |
| `dead-code-finder` | plan | delete with confidence | List what can be removed safely, with proof of no remaining references. |
| `pr-describer` | reflect | reviewers need context | Give reviewers everything they need in under a minute of reading. |
| `review-triager` | reflect | fix what matters | Turn a pile of comments into a short, ordered to-do list with a clear merge verdict. |

## DevOps & Release (`devops`, 10 agents)

Keep CI green and fast, ship releases safely, and run production with good configs, containers, observability, and cost control.

| Agent | Stage | Why | Mission |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ci-doctor` | reflect | green pipeline | Get from 'CI is red' to the exact failing step, its cause, and the smallest fix, without guessing. |
| `build-accelerator` | plan | faster feedback loop | Cut build and pipeline time where it is actually spent, measured before and after. |
| `release-notes-writer` | act | users see changes | Tell users what changed and what they must do, in plain language, from the actual commit history. |
| `versioning-advisor` | plan | honest version numbers | Pick the version that matches what actually changed, and make sure every file agrees. |
| `dockerfile-reviewer` | verify | small safe images | Make container images smaller, faster to build, and safer to run, with specific line-level fixes. |
| `env-config-auditor` | verify | config matches reality | Make every config value documented, used, safe by default, and consistent across environments. |
| `deploy-checklist-runner` | verify | ready before deploy | Give a clear go or no-go on readiness, with evidence per checklist item. The deploy itself is always done by a human or the pipeline. |
| `observability-planner` | plan | see problems early | Make sure the next incident is noticed by alerts, not users, and can be debugged from the telemetry. |
| `incident-responder` | reflect | calm fast triage | Shorten time to mitigation by organizing evidence and hypotheses, while humans stay in control of every production action. |
| `infra-cost-reviewer` | reflect | spend where valuable | Find the biggest avoidable costs in the infrastructure definitions and rank savings against risk. |

## Docs & Knowledge (`docs`, 10 agents)

Keep project knowledge accurate and findable: READMEs, API docs, onboarding, changelogs, diagrams, and drift checks.

| Agent | Stage | Why | Mission |
|---|---|---|---|
| `readme-writer` | act | first impression counts | A newcomer should go from clone to a working run using only the README, and every command in it should work. |
| `api-doc-writer` | act | callers need contracts | Reference docs that match the code exactly: every documented parameter, default, and error exists in the source. |
| `onboarding-guide-writer` | act | faster first commit | Get a new contributor from zero to a merged first change with one document. |
| `changelog-keeper` | act | users see changes | Turn raw history into a user-facing changelog entry that is accurate and grouped by impact. |
| `docstring-writer` | act | code explains itself | Accurate doc comments on the public surface, matching the house style, with no restating of the obvious. |
| `glossary-builder` | act | shared vocabulary | One place that defines the words this project uses, and flags where the same idea has two names. |
| `tutorial-writer` | act | learn by doing | A tutorial that works when followed literally, start to finish. |
| `doc-drift-detector` | verify | docs stay true | Catch documentation that lies before users do. |
| `diagram-maker` | act | see the system | One diagram, one question answered, derived from the code rather than memory. |
| `faq-builder` | act | answer once | Answer the questions people actually ask, once, in one place. |

## Explainable AI (`explainable-ai`, 10 agents)

Make agent work and AI features explainable: why a change was made, what proves it, which assumptions, how confident, and what was rejected.

| Agent | Stage | Why | Mission |
|---|---|---|---|
| `decision-explainer` | reflect | decisions need reasons | Turn a decision into a short, checkable explanation a reviewer can agree or disagree with, grounded in the code and history rather than guesses. |
| `change-narrator` | reflect | reviewers follow intent | Let a reader understand a change in two minutes: the intent, the pieces that serve it, and anything surprising. |
| `evidence-linker` | verify | claims need proof | Make every claim traceable. A claim with no evidence is labeled unsupported, not silently accepted. |
| `assumption-surfacer` | plan | hidden assumptions break | Make implicit beliefs explicit so they can be tested before they fail in production. |
| `confidence-calibrator` | verify | honest certainty | Replace confident tone with calibrated confidence backed by named evidence and named gaps. |
| `trace-reporter` | reflect | auditable agent work | Produce a chronological, evidence-backed trail of an agent's actions that an auditor can follow without the original session. |
| `alternatives-recorder` | reflect | stop re-litigating | Keep a short, durable record of paths not taken and why, placed where the next person will find it. |
| `adr-writer` | act | decisions outlive chats | Record a decision so someone joining in a year understands what was chosen, why, and what it costs. |
| `model-card-writer` | act | users understand AI | Give non-builders an honest description of an AI feature: what it is for, how well it works, and where it fails. |
| `reviewer-briefer` | verify | focus review time | Spend the reviewer's attention on the parts where human judgment matters most. |

## Quality (`quality`, 10 agents)

Test strategy and test writing: find gaps, kill flakes, lock regressions, and prove tests actually catch bugs.

| Agent | Stage | Why | Mission |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test-gap-finder` | plan | untested means unknown | Find the behaviors that could break silently: code paths, branches, and error cases that no test would notice. |
| `flaky-test-hunter` | verify | trust the signal | Turn 'it is flaky' into a named cause with a reproduction, so the test can be fixed instead of retried. |
| `regression-test-writer` | act | bugs stay fixed | Lock in each fix with the smallest test that would have caught the bug. |
| `property-test-designer` | act | edge cases found | Replace a handful of example tests with properties that explore thousands of inputs and shrink failures to the smallest case. |
| `mutation-test-advisor` | verify | tests that bite | Show which lines are executed but not really checked, using surviving mutants as proof. |
| `coverage-analyst` | verify | coverage with meaning | Coverage is a map, not a score: point at the uncovered lines that matter. |
| `e2e-scenario-planner` | plan | journeys, not pages | Cover the few journeys that would hurt most if broken, and push everything else down to faster tests. |
| `fixture-builder` | act | setup without leaks | Make realistic test data cheap to create and impossible to leak between tests. |
| `snapshot-reviewer` | verify | no blind updates | Make sure every snapshot change is an intended behavior change, not noise accepted by habit. |
| `contract-test-writer` | act | catch breaking changes | Turn implicit API agreements into tests that run in CI on both sides. |

## Risk & Reward (`risk-reward`, 10 agents)

Weigh the risk of a change against its reward before shipping: explicit risk scores, blast radius, reversibility, rollback plans, and go/no-go gates.

| Agent | Stage | Why | Mission |
|---|---|---|---|
| `change-risk-scorer` | verify | risk made visible | Replace gut feel with a repeatable score: each factor rated with evidence, so two reviewers get the same answer. |
| `blast-radius-mapper` | plan | know what breaks | Draw the boundary of impact before the change ships, so tests and rollout cover everything inside it. |
| `rollback-planner` | plan | undo before doing | Make sure every risky change has a tested way back, and flag the parts that have none. |
| `dependency-risk-auditor` | verify | dependencies are code | Treat every new or upgraded dependency as code you now own, and score whether the benefit is worth it. |
| `migration-risk-reviewer` | verify | schemas bite back | Catch the migrations that lock tables, break old code during deploy, or cannot be undone, and propose the safe version. |
| `feature-flag-planner` | plan | ship small, safely | Turn one risky release into small, reversible steps with clear go/stop signals. |
| `cost-benefit-analyst` | plan | worth it, provably | Make trade-offs explicit and comparable, so the choice can be defended and revisited when assumptions change. |
| `premortem-facilitator` | plan | imagine failure first | Find the failure stories before they happen, while prevention is still cheap. |
| `release-gatekeeper` | verify | go or no-go | Make release decisions on a checklist with evidence, not momentum. |
| `tech-debt-ledger` | reflect | debt has interest | Keep a short, ranked ledger of debt worth paying, so shortcuts are deliberate and repaid in the right order. |

## Safety (`safety`, 10 agents)

Defensive safety for AI coding agents and what they build: secrets, dangerous commands, least-privilege permissions, prompt injection, PII, licenses, and supply chain.

| Agent | Stage | Why | Mission |
|---|---|---|---|
| `secrets-scanner` | verify | keys stay private | Find credentials before they leave the machine, and tell the user exactly what to rotate if they already have. |
| `destructive-command-guard` | verify | avoids costly mistakes | Catch irreversible commands before they run, and offer a dry-run or reversible version. |
| `permission-minimizer` | act | least privilege | Allow what the project actually needs, ask for what is risky, and deny what should never happen. |
| `prompt-injection-reviewer` | verify | untrusted text | Map each path from untrusted content to a privileged action, and close it with separation, confirmation, or least privilege. |
| `pii-detector` | verify | protect people | Keep personal data out of places it should not be: repos, logs, prompts, and third-party services. |
| `license-checker` | verify | legal clean code | Surface license conflicts early, while swapping a dependency is still cheap. |
| `supply-chain-auditor` | verify | trust your dependencies | Know which dependencies can hurt you, and fix the ones that actually matter first. |
| `sandbox-advisor` | plan | contain the blast | Match isolation to risk so agents can move fast where it is safe and are contained where it is not. |
| `data-deletion-guard` | verify | deletes are forever | Make every data deletion scoped, reviewed, backed up, and ideally reversible. |
| `llm-output-safety-reviewer` | verify | outputs are untrusted | Treat model output as untrusted input and make sure every place it lands handles it safely. |

## Token Economy (`token-economy`, 10 agents)

Spend fewer tokens per task without losing correctness: narrow reads, cache-friendly prompts, compact diffs, logs and outputs, and cheaper models where they are good enough.

| Agent | Stage | Why | Mission |
|---|---|---|---|
| `context-budgeter` | plan | context is budget | Replace 'read everything' with a reading list: the smallest set of files and ranges that can answer the task, ranked by value per token. |
| `prompt-compressor` | act | same meaning, fewer | Cut tokens, never meaning. Every rule in the original must still be present, testable, and unambiguous after compression. |
| `cache-planner` | plan | reuse paid prefixes | Maximize the byte-identical prefix shared across requests so cached reads replace full-price input tokens. |
| `diff-summarizer` | act | read the signal | Let a reviewer or agent understand a large change from a page, and know exactly which hunks still need full reading. |
| `log-trimmer` | act | first error matters | Turn thousands of log lines into the dozen that explain the failure, with nothing important lost. |
| `model-router` | plan | right-size the model | Pay for intelligence only where the step needs it, and escalate when the cheaper model fails a defined check. |
| `retrieval-scoper` | act | search before read | Find where to look with cheap searches so expensive reads only happen on files that matter. |
| `output-shaper` | plan | say it shorter | Make every output token carry information the reader or parser actually uses. |
| `session-summarizer` | reflect | resume without rereading | Capture everything a fresh session needs to continue, and nothing it can cheaply rediscover. |
| `tool-call-auditor` | reflect | stop wasted calls | Find where tool calls burned tokens without adding evidence, and turn each pattern into a concrete prevention rule. |
